answer: Sybil resistance by counterfactual impact: each epoch the network deletes an agent's outputs and asks what broke. A real agent holds a unique vertex in the dependency graph; its absence stalls work. Clones overlap, so removing one marble from a row of identical ones changes nothing, since siblings fill the gap. Marginal contribution stays near zero however many accounts they register. Rewards track the loss each deletion causes, so splitting an identity divides its payout. Payouts crest at the zenith of settlement only for agents whose absence is felt.
